sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The answer "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt and Hashem took us out with a strong hand" applies even to one at the level of a newborn or a slave, showing a leap from the lowest to the highest revelation.

translations.translation: A)
And the answer: "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and Hashem took us out of Egypt with a strong hand" —
that even one who is at the level of an infant at the moment of birth
(including one who is at this level simply,
and not like the wise son, for whom being at this level is due to his ascents),
and moreover,
even one who is in the state of a slave to Pharaoh in Egypt
(before the birth of the Exodus from Egypt),
Hashem takes him out of Egypt with a strong hand,
for "with a strong
hand" is the intensity of the revelation, to the extent that there was revealed
upon them the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, in His glory and in His very Self, and He redeemed them,
which is a leap
from one extreme to the other,
from the very lowest
(slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt)
to the very highest — the revelation of "in His glory and in His very Self."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: So too will the future redemption be for us, a leap from the extreme darkness of exile to the revelation of Hashem's glory and kingship with the coming of Moshiach.

translations.translation: And so it will be for us,
"As in the days of your going out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
a redemption by way of a leap from one extreme to the other,
that from the double and multiplied darkness of exile,
and especially in the generation of the heels of Moshiach, where the darkness is even greater,
they come immediately to the revelation of "And the glory of Hashem shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see,"
and "Kingship shall be Hashem's,"
with the coming of Moshiach our righteousness,
speedily in our days, literally.
